newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parties register candidates before polls.
newsitem.headline: Polish parties register candidates before polls.

text.p: More than 20 political parties and electoral coalitions have met the deadline for registering candidates for Poland's general elections on September 21, the State Electoral Commission (PKW) said on Wednesday.
PKW secretary Kazimierz Czaplinski said nearly 6,400 candidates had registered to contest seats in the 460-seat lower house of parliament, with 497 running for the Senate (upper house).
"These numbers may increase...because we are still reviewing lists submitted at the last minute," Czaplinski told Reuters. The deadline for registration was midnight on Tuesday.

Ten groups, including the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the main opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS), registered candidates in more half of the 52 constituencies, he said.

The SLD, governing in coalition with the Peasant Party (PSL) since the last elections in 1993, is putting up 551 candidates for the lower house, the Sejm, and 84 to the Senate, spokesman Andrzej Urbanczyk said.

Most of the candidates come from the SLD alliance's core party, the ex-communist Social Democracy of Poland (SDRP), while about 100 are from the OPZZ, a trade union which had cooperated with the communist authorities before 1989.
The AWS list of more than 700 candidates is dominated by people recommended by the Solidarity trade union, the biggest of more than 30 right-leaning parties grouped in the alliance.

Recent public opinion polls show a new government after the elections will be led by either the SLD or the AWS, which are backed by more than 20 percent of voters. But smaller parties are likely to hold the balance of power.

Polls show five more parties are likely to achieve the minimum of five percent of the vote required to enter parliament: the Peasants, the centrist Union for Freedom, the leftist Union of Labour, the rightist Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland and the Pensioners' Party, which says it is centrist.
